name: Tashkent Modernist Architecture. Modernity and Tradition in Central Asia
description: Tashkent rebuilt its centre after a devastating 1966 earthquake, and this group of ten Soviet-era modernist buildings and complexes, from the 1960s to early 1990s, shows how. Museums, exhibition halls, housing blocks and scientific facilities line the new city axes. Built with prefabricated, earthquake-resistant methods, they adapt local materials and climate-conscious design to a bold concrete aesthetic.
